config.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React

intro.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that securely stores a JSON Web Token (JWT) in the browser and decodes it to display user information. You will learn the core concept of managing authentication state by storing the token in localStorage and extracting data from it. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript for building the UI, the jwt-decode library for parsing the token, and the browser's localStorage API for persistent storage. By the end, you'll have a functional component that can save a token, retrieve it, and show the decoded user details like username or email in a simple interface.
intro.usecase: JWT storage and decoding is essential for user authentication in modern web applications. When users log into platforms like banking dashboards, e-commerce sites, or project management tools, their session data is stored as JWT tokens. Developers need to securely store these tokens in localStorage or cookies and decode them to display user-specific information like profile names, permissions, or subscription status. This pattern ensures personalized experiences while maintaining security across page reloads and browser sessions.

objectives: Apply TypeScript interfaces to define the structure of decoded JWT payload data
Use the localStorage API to store JWT tokens securely in the browser
Implement token retrieval functions to access stored JWT tokens from localStorage
Execute conditional checks to verify token existence before attempting operations
Utilize the jwt-decode library to parse and extract data from JWT tokens
Construct React components with TypeScript props to display decoded user information
Define custom hooks to encapsulate JWT storage and decoding logic for reuse
Handle token expiration scenarios by implementing time-based validation checks
Return appropriate fallback values or error states when token operations fail
Assign decoded JWT payload data to component state for dynamic UI updates
Control component rendering based on authentication status derived from token data
Modify token storage approach to include sessionStorage as an alternative persistence method

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Add an import statement at the top of your file to import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the ES6 import syntax to import both React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';

steps.expectedOutcome: The file should have a valid import statement for React and useState, making them available for use in your component.
successCriteria: The import statement must correctly import both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import syntax. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Remember to use `import React, { useState } from 'react';` to import both React and the useState hook.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element. The component should be defined with TypeScript syntax.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Remember to include a return statement with some JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional App component is created with proper TypeScript typing that returns JSX.
successCriteria: Component named App is defined
Component returns JSX
Component uses TypeScript syntax (explicit return type or inferred)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component with TypeScript. This gives us a foundation to build our JWT storage and decode functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component is named exactly 'App', returns JSX, and uses proper TypeScript syntax (either explicit return type or inferred from the JSX return).
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a component named 'App' that returns JSX with TypeScript syntax.

steps.title: Initialize state for JWT token
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, declare a state variable named 'token' using useState, initialized as an empty string.
steps.hint: Use useState<string>('') to create a state variable that will hold the JWT token.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a token state variable initialized as an empty string, ready to store JWT tokens.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call that declares a 'token' variable and a setter, initialized with an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the token state variable. This will allow your component to store and update JWT tokens.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're declaring a state variable named 'token' with useState, initialized as an empty string. Check that you're using the correct syntax for useState in TypeScript.
steps.feedbackWrong: The token state variable wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState<string>('') to create a state variable that will hold JWT tokens.

steps.title: Initialize state for decoded token data
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, declare a new state variable called 'decodedToken' using useState. Initialize it with null to represent that no token has been decoded yet.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The type should be something like 'any | null' since we haven't defined the token structure yet.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state for decoded data
const [decodedData, setDecodedData] = useState<any | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a 'decodedToken' state variable initialized to null, ready to store decoded JWT payload data.
successCriteria: The code must include a useState call for 'decodedToken' initialized to null, placed inside the App component after the existing token state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created state to store decoded JWT payload information. This will be essential for displaying user data from the token.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've properly declared 'decodedToken' with useState and initialized it to null. Make sure it's inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'decodedToken' state hasn't been properly initialized. Remember to use useState with null as the initial value.

steps.title: Define handleTokenChange function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleTokenChange that takes an event parameter (type React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) and updates the token state with the input's current value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives an event and calls setToken with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleTokenChange function is defined that will update the token state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleTokenChange, take a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and call setToken with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleTokenChange function. This handler will update the token state whenever the input value changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your function: 1) is named handleTokenChange, 2) takes an event parameter with the correct type, and 3) calls setToken with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleTokenChange function is not defined correctly. Make sure to create a function that updates the token state when an input changes.

steps.title: Define decodeToken function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named decodeToken that takes no parameters. This function should decode the current token state and update the decodedToken state with the result.
steps.hint: You can create a function using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. Inside the function, you'll need to access the current token value and use atob() to decode the payload part of the JWT.
steps.expectedOutcome: A decodeToken function is added to the component that will decode JWT tokens when called.
successCriteria: The function should be named decodeToken, take no parameters, and contain logic to decode the token using atob() and update the decodedToken state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the decodeToken function. This function will handle the JWT decoding logic when we call it later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your decodeToken function properly accesses the token state and uses atob() to decode the payload part of the JWT token.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decodeToken function is missing or doesn't follow the requirements. Remember to create a function named decodeToken that takes no parameters and contains decoding logic.

steps.title: Define saveTokenToStorage function
steps.instruction: Create a function named saveTokenToStorage that saves the current token value to localStorage.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.setItem() with a key like 'jwtToken' and the token state variable as the value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that persists the token to localStorage when called.
successCriteria: Function named saveTokenToStorage
Uses localStorage.setItem()
Saves the token state variable
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a function that saves the token to localStorage. This will allow the token to persist across browser sessions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function: 1) is named saveTokenToStorage, 2) uses localStorage.setItem(), and 3) saves the current token value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function called saveTokenToStorage that saves the token to localStorage using localStorage.setItem('jwtToken', token).

steps.title: Define loadTokenFromStorage function
steps.instruction: Create a function named loadTokenFromStorage that retrieves the JWT token from localStorage and updates the token state with it. The function should not take any parameters and should return void.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.getItem('jwtToken') to retrieve the token. Check if a token exists before updating state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A loadTokenFromStorage function that retrieves a token from localStorage and updates the token state if one exists.
successCriteria: Function named loadTokenFromStorage
Uses localStorage.getItem('jwtToken')
Calls setToken with retrieved value
Checks if storedToken exists before updating
Returns void type
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the loadTokenFromStorage function. This function will retrieve the JWT token from localStorage when called.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function: 1) is named loadTokenFromStorage, 2) retrieves from localStorage with key 'jwtToken', 3) checks if the token exists before calling setToken, and 4) has a void return type.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function called loadTokenFromStorage that gets the token from localStorage and updates the token state. Remember to check if the token exists before updating state.

steps.title: Add token input field and wire onChange
steps.instruction: Add a textarea element inside the main container for JWT token entry. Set its value to the token state and wire its onChange event to the handleTokenChange function.
steps.hint: Use a textarea with value={token} and onChange={handleTokenChange}. Add appropriate labels and styling attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A textarea input field appears in the UI where users can enter JWT tokens. The input is controlled by React state and updates the token state when changed.
successCriteria: The code should include a textarea element with value={token} and onChange={handleTokenChange}. The textarea should have appropriate attributes like placeholder and rows.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a controlled textarea input for JWT token entry. The input is properly wired to update the token state when users type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some issues. Make sure you're using a textarea (not input), setting value={token}, and wiring onChange to handleTokenChange. Also check that you're using the correct event type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The textarea input isn't properly implemented. You need to add a textarea element with value={token} and onChange={handleTokenChange} inside the main container.

steps.title: Add decode button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the main container that, when clicked, calls the decodeToken function. Place it after the token input field.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with an onClick attribute that references your decodeToken function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a button wired to a handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Decode Token</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Decode' appears below the input field. Clicking it triggers the decodeToken function.
successCriteria: Button element present
onClick attribute set to decodeToken
Button placed after the input field
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will decode the JWT token when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a button with onClick={decodeToken} after the input field.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly configured. Check that you have a <button> element with onClick={decodeToken}.

steps.title: Add storage buttons and display decoded data
steps.instruction: Add two buttons for saving and loading the token from localStorage, and add a display area to show the decoded token data.
steps.hint: Create a button for saving (calls saveTokenToStorage), a button for loading (calls loadTokenFromStorage), and a <pre> element to display the decodedToken state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding UI elements and displaying state 
{JSON.stringify(decodedToken, null, 2)}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI now includes Save Token and Load Token buttons, and a formatted display of the decoded token data when available.
successCriteria: Add a button with onClick={saveTokenToStorage} and text 'Save Token'
Add a button with onClick={loadTokenFromStorage} and text 'Load Token'
Add a <pre> element that displays the decodedToken state using JSON.stringify
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the storage functionality buttons and a display area for the decoded token data. The UI now allows saving/loading tokens and shows decoded information.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some of the required elements. Make sure to include both Save Token and Load Token buttons with correct onClick handlers, and a <pre> element to display the decodedToken.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required UI elements are missing. Add two buttons (Save Token and Load Token) with their respective onClick handlers, and a <pre> element to display the decoded token data.
